title: Missing Bean? Spring Can Still Start
description:
A missing bean does not always have to stop startup.

This verified Spring example compares a required AuditPublisher with Optional<AuditPublisher>. No publisher produces Optional.empty(); one publisher produces an Optional containing the same managed instance. The service handles absence by skipping an extra notification.

Four real JUnit tests verify required-absent failure, optional-absent success, optional-present identity and ambiguity failure. Optional handles absence, not every resolution error. Keep critical security dependencies required.

Verified with Spring Framework 6.2.11 and JUnit 5.12.2. Narration is AI-generated.

pinned-comment: Optional handles a missing candidate. It does not hide ambiguity: two competing AuditPublisher beans still fail in our test. Use this for genuinely optional features, and handle Optional.empty() explicitly.
facebook-caption:
No AuditPublisher bean? This service can still start. ☕

Optional<AuditPublisher> makes absence explicit: one candidate gives a present value; no candidate gives an empty value. The service skips the extra notification when empty.

Four actual Spring/JUnit tests check startup, values, reference identity and ambiguity. Optional does not fix every resolution error. Keep critical security dependencies required.
